CategoryCreateBody.description: A top-level category takes `kind`; a child (`parent_id`) takes its parent's.
CategoryCreateBody.title: CategoryCreateBody

CategoryUpdateBody.description:
Absent fields stay; `null` clears `icon` and `color`, and `parent_id: null` makes it top-level.

No `kind`: it is fixed at creation.
CategoryUpdateBody.title: CategoryUpdateBody

ConditionBody.description:
A condition as written. The field and operator are not narrowed here: an unknown one is the
plugin's 422 `invalid_rule`, located at `conditions[i].field`, like a blank value.
ConditionBody.title: ConditionBody

ConditionOut.description: One condition of a rule; all of a rule's conditions must hold.
ConditionOut.title: ConditionOut

ErrorBody.description: The `error` object: the frontend routes on `code`, never on `message`.
ErrorBody.title: ErrorBody

PartnerOut.description: The other leg of a paired transfer: where, when and how much.
PartnerOut.title: PartnerOut

RuleOut.description: A rule; exactly the target id `sets` names is set.
RuleOut.title: RuleOut

RuleUpdateBody.description:
The rule as it should be: every condition is stated (absent means none).

`sets` may be restated but never changed (422 `invalid_rule`).
RuleUpdateBody.title: RuleUpdateBody

SourceTransactionOut.description: An entry's source transaction as the UI and rules read it; never the raw record or the hash.
SourceTransactionOut.title: SourceTransactionOut

SourceUpdateBody.description: Absent fields stay; `purpose: null` or blank clears it. Never the account (422).
SourceUpdateBody.title: SourceUpdateBody

TagApplyBody.description: The list's filter vocabulary (`GET /api/ledger/entries`) as JSON, plus the apply controls.
TagApplyBody.title: TagApplyBody

TagUpdateBody.description: Absent fields stay; `color: null` clears the colour.
TagUpdateBody.title: TagUpdateBody

UnitCommitOut.description: Everything the commit touched, as rows (architecture §4.1): the client patches what comes back.
UnitCommitOut.title: UnitCommitOut

UnitDraftEntryIn.description:
One entry the draft changes. `description` and `note` are left as stored when absent and emptied when
null. A new entry (negative `id`) names `source_entry_id`, a stored entry of the source it splits, and
carries its `amount`; the source's original entry is the residual and takes no amount of its own.
UnitDraftEntryIn.title: UnitDraftEntryIn

UnitDraftIn.description:
The draft of the unit anchored on `anchor_entry_id`. `versions` map an entry id to the version the
client saw, for every entry of the unit (a commit carries them; a preview ignores them).
UnitDraftIn.title: UnitDraftIn

UnitFieldDraftIn.description:
`keep`: untouched (a commit accepts what resolution makes of it). `fixed`: the user's `value` (null
leaves the field empty). `reresolve`: the passes decide this field again.
UnitFieldDraftIn.title: UnitFieldDraftIn

UnitFieldOut.description: One derived field of a row as the draft leaves it.
UnitFieldOut.title: UnitFieldOut

UnitKeyOut.description: A derivation key: the pass and its basis (a `user` key's basis is the proposal it accepted).
UnitKeyOut.title: UnitKeyOut

UnitPreviewOut.description: What committing the draft would do. Nothing was written.
UnitPreviewOut.title: UnitPreviewOut

UnitProblemOut.description: A way the result would break an invariant (a commit is refused for it): a code, never prose.
UnitProblemOut.title: UnitProblemOut

UnitShownBasisIn.description: The key of the proposal the client showed for a value (`pass` is history, llm or matcher_proposal).
UnitShownBasisIn.title: UnitShownBasisIn

UnitSplitOut.description: One source transaction's allocation: the residual is its original entry.
UnitSplitOut.title: UnitSplitOut

UpdateBody.description:
Absent fields stay; `null` clears `external_ref`, `note`, `icon` and `color`.

No currency: it never changes.
UpdateBody.title: UpdateBody

post.description:
Write the draft in one transaction, then settle. A commit does not confirm: settling does.

409 `conflict` names the entries whose version moved (or that `versions` omitted); 409 `unit_moved` is a
closure that changed under the locks; 409 `stale_reference` a category, payee or account that no longer
exists; 409 `try_again` a deadlock lost twice. 422 carries the code of the first problem the preview would
list (all of them in `details.problems`), or `invalid_draft`.
